server.instructions:
CandleStack is a lab for experiments on financial time series: a user uploads a trading model (Keras or ONNX), describes its input in a manifest and backtests it on market data, crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca, then compares the results and publishes the good ones.

You act as the user whose API key signed in. The key's scopes decide which tools work: read (everything that only reads), backtests, models and publish. Call get_me first to see who you act for and what the key may do. A tool that changes data says so in its annotations.

A failed tool call answers a problem as JSON: its type (https://candlestack.tech/problems/<slug>) names what went wrong and its detail says what to do.

Docs for agents: https://candlestack.tech/docs/agents/ and for this server: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/. The resource candlestack://docs lists every docs page and reference.

Finds instruments by symbol or name: every Binance spot pair that trades (market crypto) and every tradable US stock and ETF at Alpaca (market stock). Use it to turn what the user names (bitcoin, Apple, SPY) into the instrument ID the other tools take.

The best match comes first: the most traded pair of a crypto asset equal to the query (btc finds crypto:BTCUSDT), then the exact symbol, symbol prefixes, words of the name. Each item has its last price, 24 h change and volume, and since when it has candles. Page with offset while next_offset is not null. For the most traded instruments or the top gainers without a query, use top_instruments.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#search_instruments

tools.description:
Closed OHLCV candles of one instrument in one timeframe, in pages of at most 500. Use it to look at the price around a trade, check a period before a backtest or compute something the backtest result does not say; a backtest loads its own candles, so do not fetch them for it.

With start: the candles from start on, oldest first; while next_start is not null, call again with start=next_start for the next page. Without start: the newest limit candles before end; call again with end=next_end for the earlier ones. Stocks have candles of the regular session only (09:30-16:00 New York); missing candles are never filled in (gaps). Counts against a per-minute limit of candle requests; ask for a longer timeframe rather than many pages.

Data terms: crypto comes from Binance spot, stocks from Alpaca (SIP, every US exchange, 15 minutes delayed). Alpaca allows its data for the user's personal, noncommercial use only: use it for the user's analysis here, never publish or pass on the stock candles.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_candles

tools.description:
Starts a backtest for every combination of `base` (the setup of one backtest) and the values in `vary`: models (each model's manifest sets what it reads and its timeframe, so list models to vary those), instruments, periods and decision rules, 2 to 20 backtests. All go to the end of the user's queue, which runs one at a time, or none does. `metric` is the statistic the ranking orders by.

Answers the sweep: its ID, each backtest's ID, status and setup, and the progress. Follow it with get_sweep until `done`. The backtests are ordinary ones, with the sweep's ID.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#run_sweep

tools.title: Run a sweep

tools.description:
A sweep of the user: how many of its backtests are queued, running, finished and failed, each backtest's ID, status and setup, and once none is queued or running (`done`) the ranking, best first, by `metric` or else the sweep's own. Values that read the same in the app share a rank, and the best and the worst are marked as the Compare page marks them.

Call it again while it runs; a backtest takes a minute or a few. For every statistic of the backtests, compare them with their IDs.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_sweep

`queued` (it waits for the user's running backtest to end), `running`, `finished` (it
has results) or `failed` (it has an error, also when it was cancelled before it ran).
BacktestStatus.title: BacktestStatus

Period.description: The test period `[start, end)` in UTC epoch seconds of a candle's open.
Period.title: Period

Representation.description: What the model reads: Renko bricks, a Kagi line or time windows of candles.
Representation.title: Representation

error.description: What went wrong, for a failed one
error.title: Error

number.description: The user's own number, shown as #N
number.title: Number

queue_position.description: Where a queued backtest is in the user's queue: 1 starts next
queue_position.title: Queue Position

SweepMetric.description: A statistic of `results.stats` the ranking can use: one that is better higher or lower.
SweepMetric.title: SweepMetric

SweepProgress.description: How many of the sweep's backtests have each status.
SweepProgress.title: SweepProgress

mark.description: `best` or `worst` as `GET /api/v1/compare` marks it, else null
mark.title: Mark

rank.description: 1 for the best; values that read the same in the app share a rank (1, 1, 3); null without a value (failed, or the statistic is undefined)
rank.title: Rank

SweepRanking.description: The backtests by one statistic, the best first, those without a value last.

better.description: Which way is better: `lower` for a fall by its size and for the fees
better.title: Better

SweepRanking.title: SweepRanking

SweepSetup.description: What one backtest of the sweep runs on and with.

model_name.description: Its name when the sweep started
model_name.title: Model Name

rule.description: The decision rule, as `decision.rule` of the result document
rule.title: Rule

SweepSetup.title: SweepSetup

outputSchema.description: A sweep: its backtests, how far they are, and once all ended the ranking.

done.description: None of its backtests is queued or running
done.title: Done

ranking.description: Null until every backtest ended. For every statistic, the setups and the curves, ask `GET /api/v1/compare` with the IDs of `backtests`

outputSchema.title: SweepOut
